findings: The captured dual-texture draw divides UV by W. Inactive raster slots previously held zero, causing 0/0 and a global lookup rejection despite valid covered pixels. Copying a device-selected live fragment into inactive input slots avoids those nonexistent shader invocations without altering the device coverage mask.

A corrected replay decoder routes multiple resources through the general executor. Linked against the old v133 library it reproduces the lookup failure; the same decoder linked against v134 passes. The clean v136 replay matches scalar, CPU and NPU bytes exactly.

SM4 x/y derivatives use aligned 2x2 quads and device Gather/Subtract nodes. Helper pixels are interpolated outside the primitive/scissor; whole inactive quads clone a live quad. Odd targets and partial batches retain bounded writes and masks.
The captured 200-word DWM shader passes direct CPU/NPU and scalar-quad checks. A separate analytic test checks nested derivatives and actual raster scheduling.

The first v136 qualifier used the wrong texture-test CLI syntax; baseline v133/v134 reject it too. The resumed qualifier uses --backend NPU and passes active nonfinite rejection and inactive-branch checks. Failed logs are preserved.
NPU qualification also covers ordinary textured triangles, typed loads, 53 DDI draws and an ABI8 derivative-only packet. This is component qualification, not desktop completion.
